root_cause: A regression test used a regular expression to verify a fixed GitHub Actions expression containing ${{ ... }} syntax. Regex metacharacters in the literal made the assertion fail although the workflow contained the intended concurrency expression exactly.
symptom: Powerhouse Skill Projection failed on PR #3096 while the logged workflow text visibly contained the expected CodeQL concurrency group.
fix: Replace the regex assertion with literal string containment for the exact GitHub Actions expression and preserve the existing workflow behavior.
prevention: Prefer exact string containment or equality when asserting fixed GitHub Actions expressions.
Use regex only when semantic pattern matching is required and all metacharacters are deliberately escaped.
When mismatch output visibly contains the expected literal, validate the test oracle before changing working workflow logic.
Measure fan-out changes after protected merge by enumerating runs on the exact resulting main SHA.
evidence: PR #3096 head d51682668d1551a4ffb55449154dd15ce022c070 failed Skill Projection on the regex assertion.
The emitted workflow contained group: powerhouse-codeql-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref_name }} exactly.
The corrected literal assertion landed on head aa969daa38649049abafd61b2e4344859005655a and PR #3096 protected-merged as e8054fc35dc2d824afa87a417790a2c3e073062f.
Post-merge exact-main observation showed seven runs and no broad production fan-out for the workflow/tests/docs/Brain-only change.
